Subject: Production: sudden p99 spikes — timeouts and increased 504s

Markus,

We started seeing elevated p95/p99 for the /generate endpoint around 08:40 PST. Our customers are seeing intermittent 504s and aborts; throughput is nominal but tail latency has doubled. Attaching a short trace and the top error IDs.

Example trace id: 3f2b6a1e-7c4b-4f2c-a2e9-4c9d8c1b77a1

- p99 jumps from ~180ms to 720–1,200ms for many requests

Team — forwarding FintechHQ escalation. Customer reports p99 spikes and queue_depths rising (~120), producing 504s. They flagged the trace above.

Initial ask: urgent triage + mitigation (they want an ETA).

Quick context: we rolled a small hosting config update last night that touched default batching thresholds for hosted-api (reduced batch granularity to improve throughput on long sequences). I suspect batching/queue-depth interactions with KV cache behavior may be causing backpressure on their request path.

Please triage and propose an immediate mitigation path: config rollback OR per-customer routing to low-latency pool + temporary config tweaks. Keep me posted; I'll coordinate with the customer.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:41:03 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden p99 spikes — timeouts and increased 504s

Markus — digging in now. Quick notes from initial logs (Datadog + request traces):
- Cluster: hosted-pool-12 serving FintechHQ traffic.
- Observed queue_depth growth starting 08:36 PST; sustained >100 for ~18 minutes.
- Batching metrics: average batch size increased (due to lower discard rate), but max_batch_wait_ms has grown for many requests (we saw 8–12ms instead of usual 2–4ms).
- KV cache churn: prefix cache eviction correlates with longer token decode time for some model variants.
- CPU/GPU utilization moderate (not saturated), suggests per-shard request queuing and longer scheduler delays rather than pure HW shortage.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing (short term, minutes):
1) Reduce max_batch_wait_ms for hosted-api default from 8ms -> 2ms for pool-12 (should cut tail for low-latency queries).
2) Enable per-customer bypass routing for FintechHQ to route to a small pre-warmed low-latency worker group (no large batch pooling).
3) Temporarily increase max_concurrent_requests per worker for pool-12 by 20% (to lower scheduler queueing).
4) If safe, revert last night's batching tweak (we should be careful — this is config for all tenants).

I have prepared a patch with the suggested config diffs (batch_config_diff.patch). I'm attaching a p99 chart and a short log bundle (redwood-logs-fintechhq-20261109.tar.gz) to this thread.

I'll start applying (1) and (2) once we have sign-off from Ops.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:28:05 -08:00
Subject: RESOLVED: Hosted API tail latency — mitigation applied and monitoring

Olivia / team — quick update and summary:

What we did (completed by 13:10 PST):
- Reduced max_batch_wait_ms for pool-12 from 8ms -> 2ms (config server change).
- Added per-customer routing: FintechHQ traffic routed to pre-warmed low-latency worker subset for 90 minutes.
- Increased max_concurrent_requests on pool-12 workers by 20%.

Immediate result:
- Observed p99 drop from ~820ms pre-mitigation -> ~210ms within 6 minutes of change (see attached p99_latency_chart.png).
- Queue_depth metrics reduced from peak ~130 -> median ~12.
- No increase in 5xx rates after change; we monitored both error rate and throughput for one hour.

Next steps (post-mortem + durable fix):
- Root cause: interaction between our recent batching-granularity tweak and per-tenant request patterns produced larger-than-expected batch wait growth and KV cache churn, causing scheduler queueing.
- Action items: revert the default batching tweak for hosted-api while we ship adaptive batching (SUP-2384), add per-tenant backpressure controls, and implement an early-warning alert for sustained queue_depth > 40.
- Owner: Rishi + Dev to drive infra changes; Marissa to coordinate customer comms and crediting if required.

Attachments: p99_latency_chart.png, redwood-logs-fintechhq-20261109.tar.gz, batch_config_diff.patch

Thanks for your patience — we'll follow up with a full post-mortem and timeline for the adaptive batching deliverable.
